newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alfa cash flow impresses in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Alfa cash flow impresses in first quarter.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Alfa SA posted impressive first quarter cash flow, particularly when the focus is on the company's dollar earnings, analysts said.
ALFA on Thursday posted a net income of 910 million pesos in the first quarter, or 1.52 pesos per share on the 600 million oustanding shares on March 31, it said.
"It was a good result, but focusing on cash flow in dollars it was a record result," Robert Fleming company analyst Terry Sigler said.
The Monterrey-based conglomerate reported that net sales revenues fell 9.1 percent in the first quarter to 7.146 billion pesos compared to the same quarter of 1996.
But in dollar terms, first quarter revenues rose 9.1 percent over the same year-earlier period to $894 million.

So while the company produced more and sold more, that was not enough to offset a decline in real selling prices in pesos caused by a stronger peso and a reduction in international selling prices for some of its commodity products, the company said in a statement.
ALFA has five divisions: steel (Hylsamex), petrochemicals (Alpek), food (Sigma), telecommunications (Onexa) and retail and auto parts (Versax).

Goldman, Sachs & Co analyst Kerry McHugh said in a report that, "The better-than-expected results were driven by Hylsamex, which reported EBITDA of $81 million U.S., well ahead of our estimate of of $73 million U.S., on the back of very strong total shipments (659,000 versus our estimate of 606,000)."

The company said the slow growth in peso sales was a result of seasonally lower sales at Sigma, decreased activity in Mexico during the Easter Week and a decrease in average selling prices by 4.5 percent due to the strong peso.
Sales volumes improved on a year-over-year basis in the quarter as the economy improved and ALFA increased production capacity, it added.

In the first quarter ALFA generated a record high earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), of $197 million for the quarter, 9.0 percent above the $181 million in the fourth quarter.
Still, the company showed a large decrease in net income compared with the first quarter of 1996, when peso appreciation artificially overstated net income for non-cash reasons, McHugh said.
The company said its revenues in peso terms were affected by 5.6 percent inflation and 0.4 percent nominal devaluation of the peso in the quarter.
"Overall on an operating basis the results were good, but there were two negative effects," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
They were the lower monetary gain, on Mexican accounting rules, as the peso did not weaken enough to offset inflation, and also the weaker international chemical prices, the analyst said.
The company said that exports in the first quarter rose 14.6 percent over the last quarter of last year, to $230 million, or 25.3 percent of revenue.
The company said that a combination of a strong cash generation and healthy interest coverage is allowing it to continue its aggressive expansion plans.
"These investments will boost ALFA's earnings as they come on stream in the future," it said.
